xs-hacking(7) ​

Contributing

Build and test xs, find your way around the source, and keep this manual in step with the code.

BUILD AND TEST ​

sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build
XSYNC_FALLBACK=0 python3 tests/difftest.py                         # differential corpus vs rsync
XSYNC_FALLBACK=0 python3 tests/difftest.py --xsync tests/xs-noclone.sh  # forced byte copies
cmake --build build --target filter_test xattr_value_test sparse_test
build/filter_test && build/xattr_value_test && build/sparse_test

Most Python tests take the binary from XSYNC_TEST_BINARY (default build/xs), clear personal defaults with XSYNC_CONFIG='' XSYNC_OPTS='', and compare against the rsync named by XSYNC_TEST_RSYNC or the first one on PATH. Remote cases run through tests/fakessh.sh unless tests/ssh-rig.sh provides a real sshd. Run any test file directly, for example python3 tests/output_test.py -v.

tests/fixtures/protocol3.tar.gz is the frozen protocol-3 source used by protocol_test.py. Never regenerate it; add a new fixture when the supported version window moves (adding a feature).

SOURCE LAYOUT ​

FileResponsibility
common.hShared types, version and protocol constants, feature bits, options and global state.
engine.h, pool.hEntry points of the local, client and server engines and what they share; the two-queue worker pool.
main.cppHelp and version text, option parsing, signals, the final summary, and dispatch to an engine.
arguments.cppMerges personal defaults into the effective argument list.
fallback.cppKeeps the original arguments, stdin and umask so a real rsync can be run instead.
transport.cppParses [user@]host:path and rsync://, splits shell words, picks the remote shell.
install.cpp--install HOST: detects the platform, chooses the release, installs atomically.
local.cppThe same-machine engine: parallel scan and copy, plus shared setup.
remote.cppThe wire protocol: framing, negotiation, sender, receiver and the client/server glue.
fs.cppFilesystem primitives, directory listing and the receiver-side generator and writer.
destination.cppEvery receiver-side operation, relative to an anchored directory, without following symlinks.
names.cppCase-folding and Unicode name equivalence on the destination, via ICU.
listing.cpp, selection.cppSource listings; --files-from parsing and selected directories.
filter.cpprsync filter rules, merge files and CVS rules, with separate sender and receiver decisions.
delta.cppStreaming block matching for local copies and negotiated remote deltas.
hardlink.cpp, link_dest.cpp, sparse.cpp-H link groups; --link-dest snapshot reuse; sparse writes.
permissions.cpp, ownership.cpp--chmod rules; --chown mapping.
acls.cpp, xattrs.cpp, xattr_value.cppNative ACLs on Linux and macOS; extended attributes; bounded attribute storage that spills to a temporary file.
output.cpp, progress.cppItemize and --out-format output and logs; the live display and JSON events.
rate_limit.cpp, util.cppThe --bwlimit token bucket; global state, error reporting and number formatting.

THIS MANUAL ​

The manual lives in sites/xsync and builds with VitePress. Facts that the code defines are generated rather than written by hand, and npm run check fails when any of them drift:

  • From the binary: the option tables (xs --help), the manpage, the terminal recordings and every captured example.
  • From the source: exit codes, protocol constants, feature bits, frames, and the lists of accepted and delegated options.
  • From the repository: development status (the backlog.md tier tables), benchmark results (benchmarks/results/) and the changelog.
  • Curated: workflow pages and notes in content/*.md and scripts/*_notes.py. These are fingerprinted against the README and benchmark README, so a changed source flags the pages to re-read.
sh
cd sites/xsync
npm ci
npm run docs:refresh                 # help, manpage and derived inputs from ../../build/xs
python3 scripts/capture-examples.py  # rerun every documented example
python3 scripts/capture-output.py    # terminal recordings for the product page
npm run build && npm run check       # commit, then run check again to prove the build reproduces

Two examples need an older helper, built with cmake -S ../.. -B /tmp/xs-old -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-DXSYNC_PROTOCOL_FEATURES=127. Pass it as --old-helper /tmp/xs-old/xs; without it, those two keep their previous capture. Captures need setfacl, jq and rsync. After re-reading pages whose sources changed, npm run docs:review records new fingerprints.
